title: A telescope made of ice: the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics

questions.prompt: A high-energy neutrino (100 TeV) crosses a whole kilometre of ice. What are the odds it hits anything on the way?
feedback: Far rarer than that: in our toy model, about one in 65,000 at 100 TeV.
Closest: in our toy model, about one in 65,000 at 100 TeV.
Not that rare: in our toy model, about one in 65,000.

questions.prompt: Same patch of ice (1 km²), strings twice as far apart, so a quarter as many. How much worse does our toy telescope aim? (1 TeV muons)
feedback: Worse than that: in our toy model, more than five times worse (5.6x) with a quarter of the strings.
Yes: in our toy model, more than five times worse (5.6x) with a quarter of the strings. Trend only, not IceCube's real aim.
Not that much: in our toy model, about 5.6 times worse.

questions.prompt: IceCube records about 100,000 neutrinos a year. How many come from outer space?
feedback: Far fewer: about a hundred a year, the Nobel Committee says.
Fewer still: about a hundred a year, the Nobel Committee says.
Yes: about a hundred a year, the Nobel Committee says. Most of the rest are made in our own atmosphere.
